articles.author: uni928
articles.description:
Introduction


ChatGPT has become a powerful ally for generating HTML and other code snippets. However, if you’ve ever tried working with the HTML code it outputs, you might have run into a small but persistent annoyance.
To preview the HTML, we typically need to:
・Manually create an .html file
This process may not be complex, but doing it repeatedly can become surprisingly tedious.
To reduce that friction, I created a small web tool that lets you paste HTML code and instantly render it in the browser—without saving any files.
🔗 Try it here
Copy the HTML code generated by ChatGPT
Paste it into the input field on the tool’s page
Click the “Render” button
That’s it. The entire page will be temporarily replaced with your HTML content. No need to create or save any files manually.
This tool uses document.write() to replace the document with your input. If your code contains syntax errors, the browser will usually provide helpful messages, and the line numbers in the console log remain consistent with your input. This makes debugging a bit easier as well.
Opening and saving HTML files manually each time you want to make a change might seem trivial at first. But over time, it adds up and slows you down—like a slow-draining battery.
With this tool, I hope to make your workflow just a little more efficient and enjoyable.
Thank you for reading, and happy coding!
articles.title: I Created a Simple Tool to Instantly Preview HTML Generated by ChatGPT

Outsourcing your app idea can save serious time and money—if you do it right.
I wrote a full breakdown here:
5 Best Tips When Outsourcing an App Developer
If you’re building an MVP, this will help you avoid common mistakes and build faster.
Here’s a short version for quick reference:
Define a Clear MVP Scope


Pick the Right Outsourcing Model



Freelancers: great for quick MVPs
Agencies: better for structure and scale
Dedicated Teams: best for long-term builds
Vet More Than Just Code
Good communication > fancy tech stack.
Look for:
Live apps in their portfolio
Quick, clear replies
Smart questions
Break the Work into Milestones
Weekly check-ins work best. Use tools like:
Trello/Jira for task tracking
Figma for designs
Loom/Zoom for progress demos
Protect Your IP and Budget
Sign contracts and NDAs
Set clear payment milestones
Host the code in your own Git repo
Wrap-up
If you're launching something new, focus on MVP first. Test fast. Learn faster.
And if you’re outsourcing, plan smart and stay in control.
